name: The Gates of the Old River
region_detail: Along a disused branch of the Storbruhn, removed from the present commercial channel.
site_type: lockworks | Abandoned infrastructure; ancient sites | Ancient hydraulic works and associated maintenance chambers.
history: An unidentified civilization constructed a series of stone basins, channels, and immense gates to regulate the movement of water and vessels through this stretch of the river. Subsequent changes in the watercourse left portions of the works isolated from the principal channel. Their original function and the settlement they served have been forgotten.
current_state: Silt and vegetation obstruct the outer channels, but several basins retain water. During unusually high or low water, individual gates sometimes move without apparent assistance, causing water to flow through passages believed to be sealed. The surviving masonry is substantially older than nearby Cadorian infrastructure.
inhabitants: Waterbirds, fish, and other river creatures; occasional curious pilots. Any occupants of the enclosed maintenance chambers are undetermined.
danger_level: Moderate due to unstable masonry, sudden water movements, and submerged passages; other hazards are undetermined.
points_of_interest:
Stone lock basins; massive sluice gates; towpaths; partially submerged stairs; worn level markings; inspection shafts; maintenance chamber entrances.

Unresolved elements: The identity of the builders and the original purpose of the works; Whether the gates operate mechanically, magically, or through an unknown caretaker; The destination of the deeper channels; Whether any portion of the installation can be restored to useful operation.
discovery: Along a disused branch of the Storbruhn, removed from the present commercial channel. An older river chart depicts unexplained masonry beside the former channel. Experienced pilots may recognize surviving stonework near the entrance.
related_records:
Rumor: R-WB-015 — The Forgotten Lockworks — Direct. The stone channels and moving gates are the subject of the rumor.

Notable individuals and factions: Tobin Sedge (N-029) — may recognize the old river channel; Independent river pilots and boatmen familiar with abandoned waterways.
